about.title: Upland Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Upland looks different from one block to the next. Some people spend their shifts in warehouses and shops along Foothill Boulevard, others drive service routes up Euclid Avenue and Mountain Avenue or merge onto SR-210 several times a day. When an injury happens on the clock, the first question is usually simple: who pays for this? In California, the answer starts with workers' compensation, which covers medical care and partial wages through your employer regardless of who was at fault. It is normally the only claim you can bring against the employer itself. But a second path opens when someone outside your company caused the harm — a subcontractor on a job site, a property owner who ignored a hazard, the maker of a faulty tool, or another driver. Upland recorded 430 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involved people who were working at the time. We handle workplace injury claims and can help you determine which claims apply to your situation. Our team works on a contingency basis, so there is no fee unless you recover.

items.title: We Look Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or driver can be held responsible in a separate claim. We can check for that second path in your case.

items.title: Deadlines Are Handled Early
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party claim carries a two-year filing deadline. We keep both clocks in view from the start.

items.title: Retaliation Is Not Allowed
items.desc: It is illegal for an employer to fire, demote, or punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. We can explain what to do if that starts to happen.

items.question: I was rear-ended on SR-210 while driving for my Upland employer. Is that workers' comp or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. Because another driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. We can coordinate the two so the benefits don't conflict.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: In most situations, no. Workers' compensation is designed to be the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault, in exchange for benefits that don't require proving negligence. The exceptions are narrow, which is why the focus usually shifts to whether an outside party contributed to the injury.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. We provide a free case review. Our team handles injury claims on a contingency basis, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
